name: PCM1792ADB
title: 24-bit, 192 kHz stereo current-output audio DAC with SPI/I2C control
summary: PCM1792A is a stereo 24-bit audio DAC in a 28-lead SSOP with balanced current outputs (7.8 mA p-p) meant for an external op-amp I/V and filter stage. It takes PCM at 10 kHz to 200 kHz through an 8× interpolation filter, 1-bit DSD through an analog FIR filter, or data from an external digital filter. Volume, mute, de-emphasis, filter rolloff, mono mode and the rest are set over SPI, I2C or the TDMCA serial format. Analog runs from 5 V, digital from 3.3 V, and the digital inputs take 5 V.
key_figures: 127 dB typ (2 V rms), 129 dB (4.5 V rms), 132 dB (mono)
10 kHz to 200 kHz PCM; 2.8224 MHz DSD
VCC 4.75 V to 5.25 V, VDD 3 V to 3.6 V

circuits.title: Typical connection in PCM mode
circuits.description: Stereo PCM DAC with SPI control. An audio source drives LRCK, DATA, BCK and SCK; a controller owns the SPI port (MS, MDI, MC, MDO), reset, and reads both zero flags. MSEL is grounded, which picks SPI. Each 5 V supply pin has its own bypass: 0.1 µF plus 10 µF on VCC2L and VCC2R, 10 µF on VCC1, and the two bias pins VCOML and VCOMR each take 47 µF up to the 5 V rail. IREF returns to ground through 10 kΩ. VDD is bypassed by 0.1 µF and 10 µF to the digital ground. Each of the four current outputs feeds the inverting input of its own op amp with Rf and Cf in parallel as feedback, the non-inverting input grounded, so each output is held at virtual ground and turned into a voltage; the two voltages of a channel go on to a differential-to-single-ended converter with a low-pass filter.

notes: Rf, Cf and the op amps carry no value in this circuit; the I/V output is 7.8 mA p-p × Rf.
The differential-to-single-ended converters are the stage in circuits pcm-2v, pcm-4v5 and dsd.

circuits.title: I/V and differential output stage, PCM, VOUT = 2 V rms
circuits.description: One channel of output stage for 2 V rms out, 127 dB S/N. Two NE5534s take the negative and positive current outputs into 750 Ω || 2200 pF transimpedance feedback, each with 22 pF compensation between pins 5 and 8. An LT1028 differential amplifier, 560 Ω in and 270 Ω || 2700 pF feedback and to ground, subtracts the two voltages and sets the low-pass corner, fc = 217 kHz; 33 pF from its pin 5 to the output overcompensates it. A 100 Ω resistor isolates the output jack. Every op-amp supply pin has 0.1 µF to ground; supplies are ±15 V.
notes: One stage per channel: JIM and JIP connect to IOUTL- and IOUTL+, or to IOUTR- and IOUTR+.
NE5534 pins: IN- 2, IN+ 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V- 4, BAL 5, COMP 8. LT1028 pins: IN- 2, IN+ 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V- 4, OVERCOMP 5.
VCC = 15 V, VEE = –15 V, fc = 217 kHz.

circuits.title: I/V and differential output stage, PCM, VOUT = 4.5 V rms
circuits.description: The higher-level version of the same output stage, for the best figures: 4.5 V rms out, 129 dB S/N in stereo. The transimpedance resistors are 820 Ω with 2200 pF; the LT1028 differential stage uses 360 Ω throughout with 2700 pF across its feedback and ground legs, fc = 162 kHz. Compensation, supply bypass and the 100 Ω output resistor match the 2 V rms stage. The electrical tables' 4.5 V rms and mono figures and the PCM typical-performance curves are taken at this stage's output.
notes: One stage per channel: JIM and JIP connect to IOUTL- and IOUTL+, or to IOUTR- and IOUTR+.
NE5534 pins: IN- 2, IN+ 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V- 4, BAL 5, COMP 8. LT1028 pins: IN- 2, IN+ 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V- 4, OVERCOMP 5.
VCC = 15 V, VEE = –15 V, fc = 162 kHz.

circuits.title: I/V and differential output stage, DSD mode
circuits.description: Output stage for DSD playback with a fourth-order low-pass to cut the out-of-band noise of the DSD stream, fc = 38 kHz. The I/V section matches the 4.5 V rms stage (820 Ω || 2200 pF on two NE5534s). Between it and the LT1028 sit two RC ladders: 110 Ω then 220 Ω on each leg, with 18000 pF and then 47000 pF bridging the two legs. The inverting leg then feeds the LT1028 through 68 Ω with 330 Ω back from the output and 10000 pF from its input to the output; the non-inverting leg mirrors it with 330 Ω and 10000 pF to ground. 100 Ω isolates the output jack; supplies ±15 V, each pin bypassed by 0.1 µF.
notes: One stage per channel: JIM and JIP connect to IOUTL- and IOUTL+, or to IOUTR- and IOUTR+.
NE5534 pins: IN- 2, IN+ 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V- 4, BAL 5, COMP 8. LT1028 pins: IN- 2, IN+ 3, OUT 6, V+ 7, V- 4, OVERCOMP 5.
VCC = 15 V, VEE = –15 V, fc = 38 kHz.
U3's negative-supply bypass is labelled C14, a duplicate of U2's C14; it should be C16.

circuits.title: Mono mode with balanced output
circuits.description: In mono mode both DACs run balanced on one channel's data. Each DAC's current pair drives its own 4.5 V rms I/V and differential stage; the left stage's output (OUT+) goes to pin 3 of a 3-pin balanced connector, the right stage's output (OUT−) to pin 2, and pin 1 is ground. Taken this way the output reaches 132 dB S/N.

operation.text: After the 8× interpolation filter each 24-bit sample is split: the top 6 bits become an inverted complementary offset binary code driving up to 62 levels, and the lower 18 bits with the MSB go through a third-order, five-level delta-sigma modulator running at 64 fS by default, one modulator step equal to one LSB of the upper code. The two are summed into a code of up to 66 levels, scrambled by data-weighted averaging to spread element mismatch, and drive a differential current-segment DAC. The outputs are balanced currents.

SCK clocks the interpolation filter and modulators. The part detects any SCK from 128 fS to 768 fS by itself. With the 128 fS modulator rate the clock must be above 256 fS. A low-jitter, low-noise clock source is needed for full performance; TI names its PLL1700 family as a source.

Power-on reset arms once VDD passes about 2 V; initialization then takes 1024 system clocks, after which every register is at its default. Pulling RST low for at least 20 ns does the same, with 1024 clocks counted from its rising edge; this suits systems where SCK starts after power-up. Writing SRST = 1 issues one internal reset pulse.

LRCK, BCK and DATA form a three-wire port; DATA is clocked in as BCK rises. LRCK must be synchronous with SCK but no particular phase is needed. If the two slip by more than ±6 BCK, the part reinitializes within one sample period and holds the outputs at bipolar zero until it is back in step. Formats: right-justified 16, 20 or 24 bit, left-justified 24 bit, I2S 16 or 24 bit, all MSB first in twos complement; the default is 24-bit I2S. LRCK is high for the left channel in right- and left-justified formats and low for the left channel in I2S.

ZEROL and ZEROR go high when their channel meets the zero condition (1024 frames of zero in PCM or external-filter mode; a balanced or 96h pattern held for 200 ms in DSD). PCMZ (default on) and DZ[1:0] (default off) enable the flags; ZFGL and ZFGR in register 22 read the same state. With INZD = 1 the outputs are held at bipolar zero while both channels are zero; this does not act in DSD mode.

MSEL low selects SPI. The port runs independent of SCK and the audio clocks. Each access is one 16-bit word clocked on MC while MS is low: R/W, the 7-bit index, then 8 data bits. On a read, data appears on MDO once eight clocks have passed; on a write, data is latched after the sixteenth. MS goes high between words.

MSEL high selects I2C, standard or fast mode, slave only. MC becomes SCL, MDO the open-drain SDA, MS and MDI the address bits ADR0 and ADR1 below the fixed 10011 prefix. Writes take the register address then any number of data bytes, the index stepping by one after each and wrapping from 0x7F to 0x0; an undefined register is not acknowledged. Reads use a write of the address, a repeated start and a read; the index does not step on the first read after a write. Indices 0x10 to 0x1F return data even where undefined.

Spike filtering on SCL and SDA is timed by SCK and tolerates at most two spikes in 600 ns; it works with SCK between 8 MHz and 40 MHz in fast mode. It fails in three cases: with SCK period over 120 ns, t(HI) + t(D-HD) under five SCK periods and spikes on the first half of SCL high and on SDA high just before it falls, a bit reads low; with SCK period over 120 ns, start hold time under five SCK periods and spikes on both lines during the hold, a start is missed; with SCK period under 50 ns, t(SP) longer than one SCK period and spikes on SCL just after it falls and on SDA just before, a false start or stop is seen.

Each channel has its own 8-bit attenuator, 0 dB to −120 dB in 0.5 dB steps or mute. New values in registers 16 and 17 load only while ATLD = 1. Level changes step at LRCK/1, /2, /4 or /8 per ATS[1:0]. MUTE ramps both channels to −∞ dB through 256 steps at the same rate.

FLT picks sharp (default) or slow rolloff for the 8× interpolation filter. DME turns on de-emphasis for 32, 44.1 or 48 kHz, chosen by DMF[1:0]. REV inverts both outputs; OPE = 1 forces both outputs to bipolar zero regardless of input.
MONO = 1 runs both DACs balanced on one channel's data, chosen by CHSL (left by default). Used with a balanced output it raises S/N to 132 dB.

OS[1:0] sets the delta-sigma rate to 32, 64 (default) or 128 fS. Choosing 128 fS at 44.1 kHz, 64 fS at 96 kHz and 32 fS at 192 kHz keeps the post filter's corner the same at all three rates. 128 fS is not available above 100 kHz sampling and needs a system clock above 256 fS.

DFTH = 1 bypasses the internal filter for an external one (DF1704, DF1706, PMD200 or a DSP). LRCK becomes WDCK at 4× or 8× fS, synchronous with SCK in any phase; BCK and DATA keep their roles and DATA is mono. With DFMS = 1 the part takes stereo data on ZEROL (left) and ZEROR (right). Data is right-justified 16, 20 or 24 bit by FMT[2:0]. OS[1:0] sets the modulator to 4, 8 (default) or 16× WDCK; 16× is not available above 100 kHz and needs SCK above 256 fS.

DSD = 1 takes 1-bit DSD data from an SACD decoder. DATA becomes the left input DSDL, LRCK the right input DSDR, SCK the bit clock DBCK, and BCK must be held low. An analog FIR filter removes out-of-band noise; DMF[1:0] picks one of four responses (FIR-1 to FIR-4) and OS[1:0] its rate (fDBCK, /2 or /4), which must be set before DSD. DSD must be set before DSD data arrives, or the part takes the stream for TDMCA and stops accepting control-port commands. The FIR gains relative to PCM 0 dB at 50 % modulation: FIR-1 −6.6 dB (fc 185 kHz), FIR-2 −6 dB (77 kHz), FIR-3 −1.5 dB (85 kHz), FIR-4 −3.3 dB (94 kHz).

The time-division-multiplexed command and audio format carries register commands and audio over one serial link, for a TI DSP McBSP or any programmable host. The part enters it by itself after two frames in which LRCK is two BCK long; for normal I2S/PCM LRCK must be 50 % duty. A frame is 32-bit packets, MSB first: a command packet, then either extended-command packets (initialization, no audio) or audio packets of 24 bits followed by zeros. The part is an IN device with two channels enabled by OPE. Up to 30 devices per chain take IDs automatically through DCI/DCO daisy-chain links, the first device having DCI tied high; a NO device goes at the end of a chain. DI is sampled on rising BCK, DO driven on falling BCK one cycle early. DCO goes high during a device's last audio channel to hand over to the next; skipped devices pass DCI on to DCO. If channels are enabled but their packets are not sent, the outputs are unpredictable.

Each IOUT pin swings 7.8 mA p-p at full scale around a −6.2 mA centre. TI names the NE5534 for the I/V converters, because its gain-bandwidth, settling and slew rate set the result, and an LT1028 for the differential stage for its low input noise. The 2 V rms stage gives 127 dB S/N; the 4.5 V rms stage 129 dB in stereo and 132 dB in balanced mono.
